original_question: Is there an action φ on S1 which is induced by a topological action Φ, but is not induced by any smooth action Ψ on R2 preserving two transverse foliations?
target_in_paper: Section 6.1, Question 6.2, which the paper explicitly presents as a reformulation of Question 6.1. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right official problem: it asks for a circle action φ that is induced by a topological planar action Φ, yet is not induced by any smooth planar action preserving two transverse foliations. That is essentially Question 6.2 verbatim. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: The acting group G is implicit in the paper and should be named: both Φ and φ are G-actions. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

In the official setup, Φ and φ are orientation-preserving: Φ:G→Homeo_+(R^2) and φ:G→Homeo_+(S^1). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The topological action Φ is not arbitrary; it must preserve a specified pair of transverse foliations F^+ and F^- on R^2, and the surrounding sentence allows these foliations to have prong singularities. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The phrase “induced by Φ” refers specifically to the action on the circle at infinity associated to the pair (F^+,F^-), not to an arbitrary boundary action coming from some compactification of R^2. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

To make the negation precise, Ψ should also be a G-action on R^2 whose induced action on the corresponding circle at infinity is exactly the given φ. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The paper frames Question 6.2 as a reformulation of the smoothability-detection question “Can we see on the induced action φ if Φ is smoothable or not?”; that conceptual framing is missing from the draft. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

There are no ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic-quantifier conditions here; the omitted information is entirely dynamical/topological. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Does there exist a group G and an orientation-preserving action φ:G→Homeo_+(S^1) such that φ is the action on the circle at infinity associated to a pair of transverse foliations (F^+,F^-) of R^2, possibly with prong singularities, induced by some orientation-preserving topological action Φ:G→Homeo_+(R^2) preserving F^+ and F^-, but φ is not the action on the corresponding circle at infinity induced by any smooth orientation-preserving action Ψ:G→Diff_+(R^2) preserving two transverse foliations? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Given a group action Φ:G→Homeo_+(R^2) preserving two transverse foliations, can one determine from the induced action φ:G→Homeo_+(S^1) on the associated circle at infinity whether Φ is smoothable? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Section 6.1 exactly. The paragraph immediately before the question fixes the missing notation by introducing a group action Φ:G→Homeo_+(R^2) preserving two transverse foliations F^+ and F^- and the induced action φ:G→Homeo_+(S^1) on the circle at infinity associated to (F^+,F^-). The paper then states Question 6.1 as a smoothability-detection problem and says “We can reformulate the question as follows,” followed by Question 6.2, which is the closest official formulation to your draft. The nearby context also records the only scope restriction mentioned there: no such counterexample exists for actions coming from transitive Anosov flows, while the nontransitive topological Anosov case remains open. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
